measuredOn.metric: corpus-f published metric (lib.ts normalizedSignalErrors, MATCH_THRESHOLD 0.01), unchanged
measuredOn.tool: pnpm exec tsx benchmarks/corpus/corpus-f/triage-detail.ts <fixture-id> [--tmax s] [--deck variant] [--reference-tmax s [--candidate ngspice]]
measuredOn.diagnosticLimitations: Fine-step runs do not establish step convergence. Reference-TMAX comparisons use each candidate's own grid and breakpoint alignment, so their maxima do not rank engine accuracy on a common grid.

rootCauses.summary: MOS1 treated CBD/CBS as constant capacitors and ignored CJ/CJSW/MJ/MJSW/PB/FC. Fixed by #601 (depletion junction charge); mosmem now matches.

MOS1 had no Meyer intrinsic gate capacitance from TOX. Fixed by #601 (Meyer gate charges). The remaining ltra2_2_line i(vs) gap was investigated under #627 (#629): it is step/grid discretisation, routed to #592.

BSIM3 (level 8, version 3.3.0, default parameters) 4-bit NAND adder. Before #624, supply and source currents were 10-40x ngspice-47 at its own points. Since the #624 b3ld.c DC-core port, spice-ts exceeds the 120 s bound. Not root-caused; tracked in #626.
The transient metric interpolates ngspice's coarse default-step output onto spice-ts points, so ngspice's own truncation and interpolation error is scored as a spice-ts mismatch.
Signals with zero or ~100 uV ngspice peaks are normalised by that peak (floor 1e-12), so fV-uV residuals exceed 1%.
BSIM1/BSIM2 (LEVEL 4/5) are not implemented. Since #552 they raise UnsupportedModelLevelError instead of silently running Level-1 equations, which caused the issue-table mismatch.
The .model VDMOS card was silently dropped. #542 made unsupported model types a typed error and #562 (#506) added the ngspice-47 VDMOS model; both VDMOS decks now match.

Capacitance-free inverter (default MOS1, no TOX/CJ, lambda 0, equal KP): v(out) jumps vertically at vin = 2.5 V (t = 5 ns); interpolating ngspice's 135-point grid across it gives 0.176 (spice-ts 3.64 V is the analytic value at vin = 2.33 V). At ngspice points: 0.0023; spice-ts default vs fine-step ngspice (TMAX 0.1 ns): 0.0030 at reference points.

spice-ts-loss (unsupported S card) at bf2e4169; runnable since #579. Ideal S/W switches make v(10), v(20), v(30), v(40) jump between consecutive output points. ngspice-47's default output on the unchanged deck has 2 us between the points that bracket every edge, and spice-ts places each edge inside that interval: v(10) crosses 0.5 V at 1.20029/3.20006 ms (spice-ts) and at 1.19856-1.20056/3.19900-3.20100 ms (ngspice). Interpolating that 2 us chord gives 0.865 (abs 0.865 V, spice-ts 1 vs ngspice 0.135 at t=1.2 ms). At ngspice points: 2.7e-20. With both engines at TMAX 0.1 us, crossing times agree within 1e-8 s, but the metric still reports 1.0 because the edge is vertical. Its max over a step edge is set by sub-step timing, not by the waveform. 8/13 signals agree to <= 5.4e-16. Recorded under #592 (metric); not counted as a match.

spice-ts-loss at bf2e4169 (dotted VERSION=3.3.0 rejected); runnable since #599. On main 68b64909 it completed in about 45 s as a mismatch: 81/90 signals over 1%. i(vcc) near t=8.95 ns was spice-ts -11.6 mA vs ngspice -25 uA (ngspice peak 275 uA), 40.6 at ngspice points, and input source currents were 7-8.7. That was a real device-level loss, not a grid artefact. On c317324f, after the #624 BSIM3 DC-core port, spice-ts exceeds the 120 s bound (2m02s wall on a lightly loaded host), so it is published as spice-ts-loss. Tracked in #626, root cause not established.
